fact: 1902年5月12日，美国矿工联合会主席约翰·米切尔动员宾夕法尼亚无烟煤区约147,000名矿工罢工（“大罢工”）；罢工持续163天，10月3日西奥多·罗斯福总统在华盛顿召集矿工与矿主代表会谈（成为首位介入劳资纠纷的美国总统），随后任命无烟煤罢工委员会仲裁；10月23日罢工结束、矿工复工。罢工期间无烟煤价格涨至每吨20美元。1903年3月22日委员会宣布裁决：矿工工资上调10%，工作日由10小时缩短为9小时，但未承认工会。

sources.title: The Greatest Strike Ever（Pennsylvania Center for the Book）
sources.quote: May 12, 1902, Mitchell called out 147,000 workers from the anthracite mines of Pennsylvania. The “Great Strike” had begun. ... With the price of coal skyrocketing to 20 dollars per ton ... With the establishment of the Anthracite Coal Strike Commission, Mitchell called off the strike on October 23. It had lasted for 163 days. ... Finally, on March 22, 1903, the Commission announced its verdict: the miners won a 10% increase in wages and a nine-hour workday. Coal was still paid by the cart load, and the UMWA was still unrecognized as a union

sources.title: Today in History–October 3: Anthracite Coal Strike（Library of Congress 藏品介绍，经 Citizen U Primary Source Nexus 转载）
sources.quote: On this day in 1902, President Theodore Roosevelt met with miners and coalfield operators in an attempt to settle the five-month-old strike; he was the first U.S. president to intervene in a labor dispute. Roosevelt appointed a commission to help negotiate terms of a settlement, which they did. Just twenty days later, on October 23, 1902, the miners returned to work.

fact: 纽约州《廉租屋法》（1901年4月12日成为法律，1901、1902、1903年三次修订，其中1902年第352章为当年修订）适用于纽约等一类城市：新建廉租屋每个房间须有窗、每两户设一室内抽水马桶、每套公寓通自来水、地块覆盖率不超过70%，多项条款同样适用于既有旧屋；该法促成纽约市廉租屋管理局（Tenement House Department）设立，该局自1902年起发布年度与两年期报告。

sources.quote: Provisions included that lot coverage could be no more than 70 percent, that there be an indoor toilet for every two families and running water in every apartment, and that there be a window in every room. Many of its provisions were made applicable to older buildings.

fact: Northern Securities Company由E.H.哈里曼、J.P.摩根与詹姆斯·希尔等人于1901年组建，资本额4亿美元，控股Northern Pacific Railway、Great Northern Railway与Chicago, Burlington and Quincy Railroad；1904年最高法院在Northern Securities Co. v. United States案中以5:4判决支持政府依据《谢尔曼反托拉斯法》解散该公司，判决执行后公司所持铁路股票按分配计划返还股东，三条铁路恢复独立经营。

sources.quote: It was capitalized at $400 million, and Hill served as president. ... the company was dissolved according to the 1904 Supreme Court ruling in Northern Securities Co. v. United States case, decided five to four. ... the company was dissolved, so that the three railroads again operated independently.

sources.quote: The new company in which Morgan and Hill held controlling interest was worth approximately $400 million.

fact: 莱斯利·肖（L. M. Shaw）1902年就任美国财政部长（任期至1907年3月；就任具体日期来源有分歧，Wikipedia记为2月1日，Miller Center记为1月7日）；其政策主张财政部在货币市场困难时注入财政资金：回购商业银行持有的政府债券、增加政府存款银行数量，并于1902年通知银行无需再为所持有的公款保留现金准备，以增加货币弹性——联邦政府对货币市场的干预在肖任内达到顶峰。

sources.title: Leslie M. Shaw (1902 - 1907)（美国财政部官网）
sources.quote: Shaw bought back government bonds from the commercial banks that owned them, increased the number of government depository banks, and, in 1902, told the banks that they no longer needed to keep cash reserves against their holdings of public funds. The intended effect of these actions was to provide a more elastic currency, which would then respond to the needs of the market. Government intervention in the money market reached its height with Shaw.

sources.title: L. M. Shaw - Wikipedia
sources.quote: In office February 1, 1902–March 3, 1907 ... Like his predecessor Secretary Lyman Gage, Shaw firmly believed that the Treasury should serve the money market in times of difficulty through the introduction of Treasury funds.

sources.title: Leslie M. Shaw (1902–1907)（Miller Center of Public Affairs, University of Virginia）
sources.quote: Shaw served at the Treasury Department from January 7, 1902, to March 4, 1907

fact: 1902年5—10月宾夕法尼亚无烟煤大罢工期间硬煤供应中断，煤价全国性跳涨：无烟煤价格从每吨约6美元一路涨至8、10、12美元，高峰期达20美元，部分城市高达30美元；密歇根州大急流城居民Gerrit Winsemius的日记记录了本地零售价与限购过程——1902年9月25日硬煤10美元/吨且每户限2吨，10月涨至12美元/吨、每户限1吨，罢工10月21日结束后回落至8.50美元/吨但仍限购半吨，12月底再记为“煤荒，12美元/吨”。

fact: 1900与1902年两次罢工前后，宾夕法尼亚无烟煤矿工的实际收益被公司体制性克扣压低：工会指控公司商店价格约为其他零售店的两倍且强迫员工购买；矿工须按每桶2.75美元从矿方购买爆破火药，而该火药实际价值仅约1.10美元；过磅时本应按2,000磅计价的煤被“称”到2,800甚至3,190磅而计件单价不变；此外还有强制医疗费与低工资等诉求。

sources.title: Bulletin of the United States Bureau of Labor Statistics No. 191 — Collective Bargaining in the Anthracite Coal Industry（1916年3月，FRASER存档）第30页
sources.quote: The grievances in which the strikers took especial interest were: (1) The company-store system, under which it was alleged that prices double those in other retail stores were charged and at which employees were compelled to buy. (2) Excessive prices for powder. (3) Excessive weight of “miner tons.” (4) Compulsory medical fee. (5) Low wages.

sources.title: Anthracite Coal Strike of 1902 — Michael Hannon（2010），明尼苏达大学法学院课程论文（引 John Mitchell, Organized Labor, 1903）
sources.quote: The miners were required by agreement to pay the operators $2.75 per keg for the blasting powder they used when it was only worth $1.10 per keg ... Instead of getting paid for 2,000 pounds of coal ore, the operators who controlled the weighing might call 2,800 pounds or even as high as 3,190 pounds a ton, while the miners were only paid the same price per ton. ... Company stores greatly overcharged for inferior goods.

fact: 1902年7月17日，布法罗锻造公司（Buffalo Forge）25岁工程师Willis Carrier为纽约布鲁克林Sackett & Wilhelms石印厂签署了一套湿度控制机械图纸，同年夏末安装冷盘管、风扇、风道、加热器与穿孔蒸汽加湿管，设计维持全年55%相对湿度、冷却能力相当于每日融化108,000磅冰，被视为现代空气调节的起点；但Carrier本人从未认为1902年这套装置算成功，除湿盘管数年后因成本原因被拆除。

sources.title: Willis Carrier — Weathermakers to the World: 1876-1902（Carrier公司官方企业史）
sources.quote: On July 17, 1902, a young research engineer initialed a set of mechanical drawings designed to solve a production problem at the Sackett & Wilhelms Lithography and Printing Company in Brooklyn, New York. ... This system of chilled coils was designed to maintain a constant humidity of 55 percent year-round and have the equivalent cooling effect of melting 108,000 pounds of ice per day. ... The drawings were dated July 17, 1902. After that, nothing would be the same. Modern air conditioning was born.

sources.title: CIBSE Heritage Group — Profile: Willis Carrier（Brian Roberts）
sources.quote: In 1902, Willis Carrier developed the first modern system for controlling a buildings temperature, humidity, ventilation and indoor air. ... Carrier never considered the 1902 installation a success, though the advertising department chose to ignore this (Heat & Cold, ASHRAE, 1997, p332). The installation was removed after a few years.

fact: 1902年8月22日，亨利·福特1901年11月创办的Henry Ford Company在福特出走后改组为Cadillac汽车公司（福特带走自己的姓名权），工程师Henry Leland说服原投资人继续造车；首辆Cadillac约于1902年10月下线（下线日期存在10月17日、10月20日等不同记载），1903年1月纽约车展展出并获得约2,000份订单。

fact: 道奇兄弟1900年在底特律开设机器作坊，为当地汽车厂生产精密发动机与底盘部件：1902年赢得Ransom E. Olds的Oldsmobile变速箱生产合同并奠定质量声誉；1903年6月16日福特汽车公司以28,000美元、12名投资者（含道奇兄弟）在底特律成立，Henry Ford选定道奇供应Model A（1903—1904）的整个底盘，据Wikipedia《Dodge》条目Ford以价值10,000美元的货物（另有记载记为10,000美元投资）向道奇出让公司10%股份；至1919年道奇从福特累计获得分红9,871,500美元，出售股份再获约2,500万美元，合计约34,871,500美元；道奇1914年开始自产整车，1916年销量已居美国第二。

sources.title: Wikipedia — Dodge（Dodge Brothers）
sources.quote: Horace and John Dodge founded the Dodge Brothers Company in Detroit in 1900, and quickly found work manufacturing precision engine and chassis components for the city's growing number of automobile firms. ... Henry Ford selected the Dodge brothers to supply a wide range of components for his original Model A (1903–04) comprising the entire chassis ... Henry offered the Dodge brothers a 10% share in his new company in return for $10,000 worth of goods ... In 1902, the brothers won a contract to produce transmissions for Ransom E. Olds' company Oldsmobile ... They had already earned $9,871,500 ... in dividends making a total return of $34,871,500 ... on their original $10,000 ... investment ... Dodge Brothers cars were ranked second in U.S. sales as early as 1916.

sources.title: Jalopnik — Bar Fights, Lawsuits and the Flu Pandemic: The War Between Henry Ford and the Dodge Brothers
sources.quote: The brothers started a machinist shop in Detroit in 1900. Their first major job was building transmissions for Ransom Olds, founder of Oldsmobile. ... They were granted a 10 percent stake in Ford Motor Company ... in 1903 they were the only ones willing to do business with Ford at all.
